subject.title: autoreview: secret-scanner false positives on identifier and member-expression values (e.g. `apiSecret: ctx.cloudinary.apiSecret`)

question: Should `secret_text_risk` treat syntactically pure identifier and member-expression assignment values as safe references regardless of identifier length or root name, while retaining fail-closed checks for literal and concrete token forms?
rationale: The current heuristic demonstrably blocks ordinary code, but broadening its safe-reference classification changes a defense against sensitive review-bundle content and requires an explicit boundary decision.

options.title: Recognize syntactic references
options.body: Accept pure identifier and dotted member-expression values only in the assignment analyzer, with positive and adversarial regression coverage preserving all literal-secret checks.

options.title: Retain the root allowlist
options.body: Keep the existing conservative scanner boundary and document the destructuring or shorthand-property workaround, accepting continued code-shape false positives.

options.title: Add an explicit override
options.body: Introduce a configuration or CLI bypass with clear incomplete-review signaling, expanding both product surface and security-policy complexity.

recommendation.title: Recognize syntactic references
recommendation.body: Accept pure identifier and dotted member-expression values only in the assignment analyzer, with positive and adversarial regression coverage preserving all literal-secret checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent merged scanner hardening and false-positive work is concentrated in this contributor's commits.
